faq: What does this tool calculate?
The input pair rounded to your chosen decimal places — round-half-up on magnitudes, applied symmetrically to latitude and longitude.
Do I need an account?
No — pair in, rounded pair out.
Can I rely on this for professional work?
The rounding itself is exact arithmetic — rely on it freely. Professional judgment enters in choosing the places, guided by the grain table.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 values assumed, like the rest of the family; rounding is datum-blind.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — fewer places can be the more honest output. This tool exists to make the honest choice easy.
Truncation instead?
Truncation biases points systematically; rounding is the professional default. If a spec literally demands truncation, it will say so — few do.
DMS inputs?
Convert to decimals first (Coordinate Converter), then round — rounding in DMS dress is a seconds decision, not a decimals one.
Half-way cases?
Rounded half-up on magnitude (away from zero) — the convention stated, which is what makes outputs reproducible.
Batch rounding?
Single pairs here; a spreadsheet's ROUND column wears the bulk, spot-checked against this tool.
Rounding and privacy?
Aggressive rounding (2–3 places) is the standard location fuzz — effective precisely because the grain is coarse.
Original value lost?
Only in the copy you paste onward. Keep the source intact — this tool dresses outputs, it does not edit archives.
